First, note that the range of $\theta =\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x$ is given by

$$
-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Now, let's take a look at the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14036892/assets/dbf36192ac332dc49ed75278838e989a37ac7d888311be1b8b059a7b59667aa6.png)

From the values in the unit circle, we see that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})=-1.
$$

However, $\frac{3\pi }{2}$ does not lie within the range of $\theta .$ To get an angle that's coterminal with $\frac{3\pi }{2}$ that lies within the range of $\theta ,$ we subtract $2\pi .$

$$
\frac{3\pi }{2}-2\pi =-\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Hence,

$$
\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-1)=-\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}10\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-1) & =10\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-5\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
